1e.note: KEY b agrees (Theta(n)) but the stored SOLUTION is wrong: selecting only the 0.2n-th order statistic and counting it misses elements with frequency >20%. Counterexample A=[1,2,3,3,3,4,5,6,7,8] (n=10): 3 occurs 3>2 times but rank-2 element is 2. Simulation: single-select wrong on 17144/100000 random arrays. Correct: run select for ranks n/5,2n/5,3n/5,4n/5 (any element with >n/5 copies must occupy one of those ranks), count each candidate: 4*Theta(n)+4*Theta(n)=Theta(n) (0 wrong on 100000); or Misra-Gries with 4 counters.
